idiom_name: librdkafka consumer that produces to a <topic>.DLT topic with failure headers before committing
implementation_notes: The C++ standard library has no messaging runtime, so the dead-letter channel is built on the client library: a Kafka consumer catches the per-record processing error, produces the original payload plus headers (source topic, partition, offset, exception, attempt count) to a dedicated dead-letter topic through RdKafka::Producer, and only commits the source offset once that produce has been accepted. produce() is asynchronous, so the commit must be gated on the delivery report (or at least on a successful enqueue plus flush) or the dead-letter hop becomes the lossy step. Where the transport is AMQP instead of Kafka, the broker's dead-letter exchange is strictly better and the C++ side is only the declaration: x-dead-letter-exchange and x-dead-letter-routing-key as table arguments, or AMQP-CPP in the same shape.
pitfalls: produce() only enqueues: committing the source offset before the delivery report (or at least a successful flush) makes the dead-letter hop lossy.
The record's key and payload buffers must be copied into the producer (RK_MSG_COPY) or kept alive until the delivery report; a freed buffer is the classic crash in dead-letter producers.
If the dead-letter producer's internal queue fills, records are dropped - dead-lettering must not share the producer with the main flow unless its queue bounds and error callbacks are configured.
Hardcoded AMQP arguments are fixed at declaration: x-dead-letter-exchange passed as a queue argument cannot be changed without deleting and redeclaring the queue.
